entries.proposition: Population-level trials are read as showing restrictive thresholds broadly safe in adult critical illness.
entries.snippet: Taken together, these trials suggest that restrictive transfusion thresholds are broadly safe at the population level.

entries.proposition: A subgroup signal of harm from restrictive transfusion in type 1 myocardial infarction is described as prespecified-subgroup, overall mortality showing no clear benefit for either strategy.
entries.snippet: In contrast, the MINT trial did not demonstrate a clear overall mortality benefit for either strategy but its prespecified subgroup analysis suggested a potential signal of harm associated with restrictive transfusion in patients with type 1 acute myocardial infarction.

entries.proposition: Impaired autoregulation (acute brain injury, fixed coronary stenosis) is the stated reason ischemia-sensitive tissue may become supply dependent at higher haemoglobin.
entries.snippet: When vascular adaptation is impaired, as in type 1 acute myocardial infarction with fixed coronary stenosis or in acute brain injury with disrupted cerebrovascular autoregulation, the ability to augment blood flow in response to anemia is constrained.9,12
entries.anchor: Circulatory flow and global oxygen balance

entries.proposition: Mitochondrial level: in one cited multicentre observational study mitochondrial oxygen tension and consumption did not change consistently after transfusion and were not strongly associated with haemoglobin or conventional perfusion markers.
entries.snippet: The investigators found that mitoPO2 and mitoVO2 did not change consistently before and after transfusion, and neither parameter was strongly associated with hemoglobin concentration or conventional markers of tissue perfusion and oxygenation.

entries.proposition: In the same study many patients had normal baseline mitochondrial oxygen tension, so the study does not show mitochondrial failure (the abstract language of 'mitochondrial failure' rests on this single measurement study).
entries.snippet: In this study, many patients had normal baseline mitoPO2 values, suggesting that cellular oxygen tension was not critically low at the time of transfusion
